label: override_express
point: Held that a Title VII disparate-pay claim is timely under 2000e-5(e)(1) only as to pay decisions within the charge period, so the employee may reach back no further than the last pay decision before that period.
change: Added 2000e-5(e)(3): a compensation practice occurs each time discriminatory pay is paid, with back pay for up to two years.
why: The paycheck-accrual rule reverses the decision's timeliness rule, and the Act's findings name the Supreme Court decision affirming it in this same case.

label: unrelated
point: A dissent footnote cited 3113(2)(B) in passing for the bar on commercial barter; the case decided which navigable waters are public lands under ANILCA.
change: Changed the period ending 3113(2) to a semicolon and added new definitions after it.
why: A punctuation change to a definition cited in passing; the law names McDowell v. Alaska, a different case.

label: unrelated
point: Upheld the Grand Canyon flight limitations rule and noise model, noting the Air Tour Management Act (40128 note) did not require a quiet-technology rule first.
change: Clarified that 40128 applies to commercial air tour operations over a national park (adding 'over a national park' throughout).
why: The scope clarification does not touch the noise methodology or quiet-technology points; the case named is Air Transport Ass'n of Canada, a different case.

label: related
point: Held that a section 2 violation is not by itself grounds to deny section 5 preclearance, while dilutive-impact evidence may bear on section 5 purpose, and remanded.
change: Rewrote 1973c to add that purpose includes any discriminatory purpose and to protect ability to elect preferred candidates.
why: The Act responds to Bossier Parish II in the same case on the purpose prong, but does not make a section 2 violation a ground for denying preclearance, so Bossier I's holding stands.

label: codifies
point: Held that amended section 207 of ILCA (2206 escheat of small fractional interests) still effected an unconstitutional taking.
change: Replaced the escheat rule in 2206(a) with a testamentary disposition scheme limiting devise to Indians and the tribe, with life estates for non-Indians.
why: Congress named the decision and replaced the escheat scheme it struck down rather than reinstating it, conforming the statute to the holding.

label: unrelated
point: Denied defendants' motion arguing the FTC had exclusive jurisdiction, citing 1333 only to describe the Labeling Act's warning requirements.
change: Rewrote the 1333 cigarette warning labels and placement requirements.
why: The new warning texts do not bear on whether FTC jurisdiction bars the RICO claims; the findings cite the later 2006 ruling in this litigation only for facts.

label: related
point: Held that the 1954 insertion of 'under God' in the Pledge (4 U.S.C. 4) and teacher-led recitation violate the Establishment Clause.
change: Reenacted the Pledge text with 'under God' (punctuation change) and changed the headdress rule to non-religious headdress.
why: Congress named and disagreed with the decision and reaffirmed the words, but a statute cannot change the constitutional rule the court applied.

label: related
point: Held that court-ordered corrective-statement onserts are not statements 'on any cigarette package', so 1334(a) does not bar them.
change: Added an exception to 1334(a) for statements the Secretary requires under the Tobacco Control Act.
why: The amendment widens permitted package statements and does not alter the onsert reading; the findings name the 2006 district court ruling in this litigation only for its factual findings.

label: override_express
point: Read 'substantially limits' and 'major life activities' strictly, relying on the 43 million finding in 12101(a)(1), to create a demanding standard for disability.
change: Struck the 43 million finding, rewrote the disability definition and directed broad construction.
why: The ADAAA rejects the decision's demanding standard and its findings name this decision as having narrowed the ADA.

label: codifies
point: Denied preclearance of Georgia's State Senate plan as retrogressive because it reduced black voters' ability to elect candidates of choice in specific districts.
change: Added 1973c(b)-(d) making diminished ability to elect preferred candidates the retrogression test.
why: The Act rejects the Supreme Court's reversal in Georgia v. Ashcroft and restores the ability-to-elect focus this district court applied.

label: override_express
point: Held that the section 5 purpose prong reaches only retrogressive purpose, so a discriminatory but nonretrogressive plan must be precleared.
change: Added 1973c(c): purpose includes any discriminatory purpose.
why: The new subsection reverses the holding, and the Act's findings and report name Bossier Parish II.

label: override_express
point: Held that 6510(a)(1) bars adding any synthetic ingredient in handling, invalidating rules allowing listed synthetics in processed organic foods.
change: Inserted 'not appearing on the National List' into 6510(a)(1).
why: The amendment permits National List synthetics, reversing the holding, and the same Act names Harvey v. Veneman.

label: codifies
point: Held that amended section 207 (2206(a) escheat) effected an unconstitutional taking.
change: Replaced the escheat rule in 2206(a) with a testamentary disposition scheme.
why: Congress, naming the Supreme Court's affirmance in this case, abandoned the struck-down escheat scheme, conforming to the holding.

label: override_express
point: On remand, granted preclearance, treating the section 5 purpose inquiry as limited to retrogressive intent (later affirmed in Bossier Parish II).
change: Added 1973c(c): purpose includes any discriminatory purpose.
why: The new subsection reverses the retrogressive-purpose limit applied here, and the Act names Bossier Parish II in the same litigation.

label: override_express
point: Held that retrogression is judged by the totality of circumstances, letting a state trade safe majority-minority districts for influence and coalition districts.
change: Added 1973c(b) and (d) making diminished ability to elect preferred candidates the test.
why: The amendment restores the ability-to-elect standard the decision displaced, and the findings and report name Georgia v. Ashcroft.
